parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a statute on the books criminalises public solicitation by males 'with intent to deceive as to true sex', a gender-presentation offence with no documented enforcement, so exposure is an open question rather than a known practice. Documents carry birth-sex markers with no change route, so every visitor carries mismatch exposure, but no border or detention outcomes are documented. Same-sex conduct law is a dead letter per 2010 and 2026 sources (tangential). No SOGI discrimination protection and no recognised relationships. One activist murder (2021) and a documented climate of fear with rising hostility, with no documented remedy or hate-crime recourse. Traditional third-gender acceptance is a real positive but is described as threatened. Thin data resolved toward the structural signals: presentation-linked offence, no recognition, no protection, no recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: Birth-sex markers on all documents, no route to change; universal mismatch exposure for visibly trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch could trigger questioning or fraud suspicion under the solicitation statute, but border practice is not documented.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented detention or custody practice for trans people; public-solicitation provision creates a possible arrest route.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Whether police apply the presentation-linked offence is unresolved, so custody exposure is open rather than known.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation; single national criminal code applies to visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not applicable beyond national code; no facility rules documented.

care_services.exposure: No documented care denial; no SOGI protection in goods or services.
care_services.protection: Single LGBTI drop-in centre and shelter, damaged by 2018 cyclone.
care_services.interaction: Shelter is a single facility, so community care capacity for visitors is thin.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Gender-presentation offence on the books; government reported no LGBT-related action; conservative framing of trans presence.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Judicial code (2010) bars bias but binds judges only.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute frames presentation as deception; this reads as state threat-framing at the statutory level.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented rules on minors; a parent travelling with a trans child inherits the same document mismatch and statute exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: No guardian recognition; a same-sex-read family has no recognised standing.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One activist murder (2021) and documented fear and hostility; no hate-crime statute documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-LGBTQ violence not documented; absence is not safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination recourse; 2010 enforcement assessment is dated.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Traditional indigenous feminine third-gender role documented as supportive, though threatened.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Cultural acceptance may soften street friction but cannot offset statutory exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: both carry universal document-mismatch exposure and a deceptive-presentation offence with no realistic remedy. This dossier is slightly higher because no detention or verification practice is documented.
Lower-exposure than 0.35-B: that anchor documents a routine police stop-and-detain pattern. Here enforcement of the presentation statute is unresolved and not documented, so the rating sits above it.

Lower than 0.55-B on the operative record: that anchor documents secondary screening and denial routes, which this dossier does not. Here, the criminal statute and absence of any recognition route add exposure the anchor lacks.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is a presentation-linked offence on the books plus universal birth-sex document mismatch with no change route, and no recognised relationship or guardian standing. These combine into a standing risk that a visitor carries whenever presenting differently from documents, even though enforcement is undocumented. Cultural acceptance (third-gender tradition) and a dead-letter sodomy statute soften the picture only marginally. Documented hostility and a 2021 murder add street-level exposure without any documented state response or remedy. Given thin data, the structural signals (criminalised gender expression, no recognition, no protection, no recourse) resolve the rating into the Elevated Risk band, above a jurisdiction with active enforcement and below one with documented universal screening and no offsetting protections.
